claim_text: On September 15, 2022, Adobe and Figma signed a definitive merger agreement for Adobe to acquire Figma for approximately $20 billion, roughly half cash and half Adobe stock.
wording_guardrail: Use approximately $20B; do not describe $20B as money actually paid because the acquisition never closed.

claim_text: The transaction required regulatory clearances and other closing conditions and the parties originally expected it to close in 2023.
wording_guardrail: Expected closing date was forward-looking, not guaranteed.

claim_text: The 2022 negotiation record shows Adobe's June 19 proposal offered $20B and did not yet include a termination fee; Figma later proposed a reverse termination fee tied to antitrust-clearance failure.
wording_guardrail: Describe as the transaction background disclosed to Figma stockholders; do not infer unrecorded motives.

claim_text: By July 20, 2022, Adobe's revised proposal included a $1 billion reverse termination fee.
wording_guardrail: This was negotiated contract risk allocation, not a later government-imposed charge.

claim_text: Section 8.2 of the merger agreement required a $1 billion cash termination fee in specified antitrust-clearance/closing circumstances and expressly stated that the fee was not a penalty but liquidated damages.
wording_guardrail: Never call the $1B a fine, antitrust penalty, damages award, or regulator-imposed payment.

claim_text: The merger agreement required reasonable best efforts to obtain regulatory approval but did not require Adobe to divest Adobe assets or Figma assets if such a Figma divestiture would reasonably be expected to be material to Figma.
wording_guardrail: Use only if explaining contractual limits on remedy actions; do not state this clause itself caused termination.
notes: Potential narrative explanation for why extreme structural remedies mattered.

claim_text: The UK CMA opened its Adobe/Figma merger inquiry on May 3, 2023.
On June 30, 2023, the CMA said it was or may be the case that the merger could substantially lessen competition and the transaction was referred for an in-depth Phase 2 investigation on July 13.
wording_guardrail: These were merger-review thresholds, not final findings of illegality.

claim_text: The European Commission received notification of the proposed acquisition on June 30, 2023, opened an in-depth investigation on August 7, and adopted a Statement of Objections on November 17.
wording_guardrail: A Statement of Objections is preliminary and is not a final decision.

claim_text: On November 28, 2023, the CMA provisionally identified competition concerns in all-in-one product design, vector editing and raster editing software.
wording_guardrail: Always use provisionally/provisional findings; never convert into a final finding that the merger was unlawful.

claim_text: The CMA's provisional remedies notice considered prohibition of the merger or structural divestitures and said divesting Figma Design would be substantially similar to prohibition but with added risks.
wording_guardrail: Possible remedies only; no final remedy or prohibition order was issued.

claim_text: Adobe and Figma strongly disagreed with the CMA's provisional findings and argued that their products and capabilities were complementary and that the transaction would be pro-competitive.
wording_guardrail: Always attribute as the parties' position; not an independent finding.

claim_text: The parties' December 14 remedies response said the CMA remedies notice effectively pointed to either prohibition or divestiture of Figma Design, which the parties characterized as effectively a full divestiture/prohibition.
wording_guardrail: Attribute 'effectively' characterization to the parties.

claim_text: The U.S. Department of Justice Antitrust Division conducted an investigation of the proposed merger and, after abandonment, publicly welcomed the companies' decision to end it.
wording_guardrail: Do not say DOJ sued Adobe/Figma or obtained a court order; Stage 01 found no such public case in the official record.

claim_text: On December 17, 2023, Adobe and Figma's boards approved a mutual termination agreement and the merger agreement was terminated by mutual written consent.
wording_guardrail: Use mutual termination/abandonment, not a final regulator order blocking the transaction.

claim_text: On December 18, 2023, Adobe and Figma said they no longer saw a clear path to obtain the necessary regulatory approvals from the European Commission and UK CMA.
wording_guardrail: This is the parties' stated joint assessment; do not convert it into a claim that a final legal prohibition had already been entered.

claim_text: The European Commission's in-depth investigation ended after the parties abandoned the transaction, without a formal Commission decision on the merits.
wording_guardrail: Do not say the EC formally prohibited the merger.

claim_text: The CMA cancelled its Phase 2 merger inquiry after the merger was abandoned; its case page is closed with the outcome 'phase 2 cancellation.'
wording_guardrail: Do not call the provisional findings a final CMA prohibition decision.

claim_text: The December 17 mutual termination agreement required Adobe to pay Figma $1 billion in cash within three business days as liquidated damages and made the payment Figma's sole and exclusive remedy under the merger agreement.
wording_guardrail: Call it contractual termination fee/liquidated damages. It was not a government fine.

claim_text: Adobe paid Figma the $1 billion termination fee on December 20, 2023 using cash on hand.
wording_guardrail: This is an actual cash payment, unlike the approximately $20B acquisition consideration that was never paid because the deal did not close.

claim_text: Figma confirms it received $1.0 billion from Adobe on December 20, 2023 and recorded the fee within other income, net.
Adobe recorded the $1 billion termination fee in operating expenses in fiscal 2024; its FY2024 filing says the fee was not tax-deductible for financial statement purposes.
wording_guardrail: Do not equate accounting treatment with a regulatory penalty.

claim_text: Figma remained independent after the abandoned merger.
Figma completed its initial public offering on August 1, 2025, selling 12.5 million company shares at $33 per share and reporting $393.1 million of net proceeds before offering costs.
wording_guardrail: Do not imply the $1B termination fee caused the IPO, IPO price, or later market value.

claim_text: The proposed $20 billion acquisition consideration and the $1 billion termination fee are distinct figures: the acquisition consideration was never paid because the merger did not close; the $1B fee was actually paid after termination.
wording_guardrail: Never write that Adobe paid $21B, bought Figma for $1B, or paid a $1B fine.

claim_text: The title formulation 'Adobe’s Failed Figma Deal Cost $1 Billion' refers to Adobe's actual contractual termination payment, not to the total all-in cost of the abandoned transaction.
wording_guardrail: If script discusses other advisory, financing or opportunity costs, keep them separate from the title's $1B core consequence.

claim_text: The CMA's November 2023 concerns and the European Commission's Statement of Objections were preliminary regulatory positions, not final findings that Adobe or Figma violated antitrust law.
wording_guardrail: Use provisional/preliminary language every time the concerns are summarized.

claim_text: The public primary record supports saying regulatory pressure made the deal untenable to the parties, but it does not support claiming that a regulator imposed the $1B payment or that a final prohibition order forced the termination.
wording_guardrail: Narrative chain: regulatory concerns + no clear path to approvals -> mutual termination -> contractual fee.

claim_text: The parties publicly maintained that the proposed combination had pro-competitive benefits even as UK and EU authorities expressed competition concerns.
wording_guardrail: Present both positions without deciding disputed antitrust merits because no final merits decision issued.

claim_text: Stage 01 found no public DOJ complaint or court judgment blocking the Adobe/Figma merger; the official DOJ source documents an investigation and post-abandonment statement.
wording_guardrail: Do not write 'DOJ sued to block the merger' unless a later primary filing is located.
notes: Negative-source finding; Stage 16 must refresh if used.
